questions.prompt: Two ideas compete for the next sprint. How do you choose which to explore?

choices.B: Compare customer impact, evidence and effort
choices.C: Pick the idea with the most votes

questions.explanation: Use the same outcome, confidence and effort assumptions to compare opportunities.

questions.prompt: Your CEO wants a feature next week. Your roadmap is full. What do you do first?

choices.A: Say yes and shift the roadmap
choices.C: Say no, the roadmap is set

questions.explanation: Starting with the problem keeps the roadmap honest.
questions.hint: Separate the request from the need behind it.

questions.prompt: An urgent request will delay your launch. What should you make visible?

choices.C: The outcome gained and the work displaced

questions.explanation: Making the opportunity cost visible lets stakeholders choose a trade-off deliberately.
questions.hint: What does saying yes mean saying no to?

questions.prompt: Your team loves a solution, but demand is uncertain. What is the best next step?

choices.A: Run a small test of the riskiest assumption

questions.explanation: A small experiment tests the risky assumption before you invest in a full build.

questions.prompt: A stakeholder pushes back when you decline a feature. How do you respond?

choices.A: Repeat that the roadmap is final
choices.B: Agree on the need and explain the trade-off
choices.C: Promise a date to end the discussion

questions.explanation: You can say no to a solution while still taking the underlying need seriously.
questions.hint: Keep the shared outcome in the conversation.
